objectives.performance: Detect and characterize missing or invalid values in a tabular dataset using Python
conditions: Given a tabular dataset loaded into a Python data structure
Access to standard Python libraries (specific library unspecified by brief)
success_criteria: Identifies all columns and rows containing missing or invalid values
Describes the type and extent of each data quality issue present

assumption_notes: Detection is treated as a distinct, assessable step prerequisite to transformation

objectives.performance: Apply transformation strategies to missing or invalid values in a tabular dataset using Python
conditions: Given a tabular dataset with known missing or invalid values
success_criteria: Applies at least two distinct transformation strategies (e.g., removal, substitution, imputation)

objectives.performance: Justify the choice of transformation strategy for missing or invalid values given a specific dataset context

assessments.capability_claim: Given a tabular dataset, detect and characterize data quality issues, apply transformation strategies, and justify each transformation choice with criterion-based rationale and explicit trade-off analysis

task.description: Given a provided tabular dataset and a brief description of its intended downstream use, the learner must: (1) detect and characterize all missing or invalid values; (2) apply at least two distinct transformation strategies such that no untreated values remain in scope; and (3) produce a written rationale for each transformation choice stating a criterion-based reason and at least one trade-off relative to a named alternative strategy. No prescribed answer key is provided.
conditions: Given a tabular dataset loaded into a Python data structure
A brief contextual description of the dataset's intended downstream use is provided
Access to standard Python libraries (specific library unspecified by brief)

rubric_dimensions.criterion: Completeness and accuracy of missing and invalid value detection and characterization
performance_levels: Identifies fewer than half of issues or characterizes them inaccurately
Identifies most issues; characterization partially accurate
Identifies all issues and accurately characterizes each by type and extent

rubric_dimensions.criterion: Correctness and distinctness of applied transformation strategies
performance_levels: Applies only one strategy or leaves untreated values in scope
Applies two strategies but they are not clearly distinct; scope nearly complete
Applies at least two clearly distinct strategies; no untreated values remain in scope

rubric_dimensions.criterion: Quality of criterion-based rationale for each transformation choice
performance_levels: Rationale absent or merely names the method without any criterion reference

rubric_dimensions.criterion: Explicitness of trade-off identification relative to a named alternative
performance_levels: No trade-off identified or no alternative named
Names an alternative but trade-off is vague or implicit
Explicitly states at least one trade-off of a chosen strategy relative to a clearly named alternative

prerequisites.rationale: The learner state records 'basic Python' as known via evidence ref research-fixture:python-data-processing:learner-state, and every assessment (asmnt-bpdp-01-formative, asmnt-bpdp-02-formative, asmnt-bpdp-summative) lists basic Python programming as a required capability with an explicit rationale requiring syntactically valid Python to interrogate structure, detect issues, and transform values. Without it the learner cannot produce runnable code for any detection or transformation task.

The learning objective (lo-bpdp-01) would fail without first acquiring detection, since transformation presupposes identification.

Candidate only. Summative assessment asmnt-bpdp-summative requires knowledge of at least two distinct transformation strategies in order to apply and compare them, and lo-bpdp-02 requires applying at least two distinct strategies. Without prior knowledge of such strategies the learner cannot satisfy the apply and evaluate objectives or the trade-off justification criterion.

modules.title: Detecting and characterizing missing or invalid values

planning_warnings.rationale: All supplied objectives are core and are retained within the 60-minute budget; each module is assigned an equal estimated portion. The planning assumption is that library-specific API instruction is out of scope outside the three linked objectives, so no optional scope reduction was required.

sequencing_rationale: Detection (lo-bpdp-01) precedes transformation (lo-bpdp-02) because lo-bpdp-02 declares lo-bpdp-01 as a prerequisite and the learner must locate issues before transforming them

Transformation (lo-bpdp-02) precedes justification (lo-bpdp-03) because lo-bpdp-03 declares both lo-bpdp-01 and lo-bpdp-02 as prerequisites, and trade-off justification depends on having applied at least two distinct strategies

Prerequisites prereq-bpdp-detection and prereq-bpdp-transformation-strategies are external capability prerequisites; the detection module aligns with prereq-bpdp-detection's teaching_objective_id lo-bpdp-01

assumption_notes: The 60-minute estimate is a provisional allocation across three equal modules; the deterministic policy decides whether module-level estimates fit the brief budget
Each module maps exclusively to a single supplied objective ID; no objective ID is placed in prerequisite_refs
Prerequisite_refs reference only supplied prerequisite IDs from the allow-list; candidate prerequisites (prereq-bpdp-detection, prereq-bpdp-transformation-strategies) remain provisional
Module lesson_ids are left empty for orchestration to derive after lesson generation

lessons.lesson_goal: Explain how to locate and categorize missing or invalid values in a tabular dataset using Python-standard inspection patterns, so the learner can later locate issues before transforming them.
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Follow a step-by-step worked example that interrogates a small tabular structure for null cells, out-of-range values, wrong-type entries, and empty rows; trace how each inspection step maps a column or row to a specific issue type and extent.

assumption_notes: Worked-example pattern is a candidate choice for analyze-level learning; demonstration followed by tracing was not evaluated
Assumes detection (lo-bpdp-01) is taught before transformation, consistent with candidate sequencing assumption
Estimated_minutes set to match the module allocation; the deterministic policy decides the final gate

lessons.lesson_goal: Enable the learner to apply at least two clearly distinct transformation strategies (e.g., removal, substitution, imputation) so that no untreated missing or invalid values remain in the targeted scope.
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Work through a pre-labeled dataset under instructor guidance, applying removal on some value locations and substitution or imputation on others, verifying after each step that no untreated issues remain in the targeted scope.

assumption_notes: Guided practice is a candidate pattern for apply-level learning; independent practice was not evaluated
Pre-labeled dataset isolates transformation from detection, matching the formative assessment design
Library-specific APIs deferred pending library confirmation

lessons.lesson_goal: Develop the learner's ability to justify each transformation choice using a criterion-based rationale (missingness pattern, data volume, or downstream use) and to state an explicit trade-off relative to a named alternative strategy.
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Work through authentic dataset-context scenarios in which a downstream use is described; for each scenario the learner states a criterion-based rationale for each transformation choice and names a trade-off against a clearly identified alternative.

assumption_notes: Scenario pattern is a candidate choice for evaluate-level reasoning with no prescribed answer key; case-based debate formats were not evaluated
No formative assessment references are supplied for lo-bpdp-03, so the lesson references none, consistent with the allow-list constraint

Integrated practice for the combined summative assessment is supplied only at the summative level; integrated formative practice was not designed because no qualifying formative assessment IDs were supplied
